projects.title: Sona PowerPredict
projects.description: IPL powerplay score prediction competition entry, team 'Byte Bouncers'. Python MyModel class iterated through versions v4 to v11. Constraints: zero hardcoded values, runtime under 10 to 20 seconds, memory under 512 MB (Docker), fully vectorized pandas/numpy. Techniques: era-decay weighting, percentile-based venue/team routing (highway/trap venue detection), five-tier wicket-bracket scoring, player intent signals from delivery data, one unified _norm() string normalization function to prevent key-matching failures.
projects.tags: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Docker, Vectorized ML

projects.title: Libre (Smart Library Portal)
projects.description: Smart Library Book Availability Portal (design stage). Students search books by title/author/subject and see availability; librarians update records. Four access levels (student, librarian, head librarian, super admin); students pre-imported from the college database and log in with registration id. QR-based issue with student photo and details on the librarian screen; edition grouping with total availability; per-copy status; shelf location and reference-only flag; bulk CSV import with ISBN auto-fill. Fines count working days (Mon to Sat) with holidays set by the head librarian; warning notice and appeal before any letter to the HOD. Note: Design and research only; not built or deployed.
projects.tags: Design & Research Only, RBAC, QR Issue, System Design

posts.title: On Wandering and Quiet Windows
posts.excerpt: Why the best stories don't arrive when you're staring at a screen, but when you watch rain wash across afternoon street corners.
posts.content: There is an art to not hurrying. In a world calibrated for instant delivery, taking three hours to walk four kilometers feels like quiet rebellion. I notice how the shadows stretch under old banyan trees, how people clutch warm paper cups, and how ordinary conversations carry unintentional poetry. These are the moments that give us back our breath.

posts.title: The Songs We Replay Too Much
posts.excerpt: An exploration of acoustic memory and why certain songs feel like small rooms where we kept our favorite versions of ourselves.
posts.content: Music has an unfair advantage over visual memory. A single chord progression can resurrect an exact temperature, the smell of roasted coffee, and an old emotion you thought you outgrew. When I keep a song on repeat for forty listens, I'm not just listening to sound — I'm trying to inhabit a particular state of grace.

posts.title: Why Mint Chocolate Chip is Undefeated
posts.excerpt: A lighthearted defense of refreshing herbal notes in frozen confectionery and why controversy is the hallmark of great taste.
posts.content: People who compare mint chocolate chip to toothpaste have surrendered their palate to convention. The initial herbal chill, followed by the slow melting warmth of dark cocoa shards, creates dynamic contrast. Great flavor, just like great life, requires a touch of contradiction.
